mission: Luke assigns Ben the Outer Rim survey — the institutional cover for a disturbance father and son have been reading independently. Both feel the wrongness; only Ben carries the years of exposure that tell him what kind of trouble it is.
why_now: Luke has been sitting on flagged survey reports for weeks. He hands Ben the mission the morning after the sparring loss, because the private problem has begun to surface where others could see it.
conflict: Luke frames the survey as a practical assignment — a Knight and a skilled pilot, not a war. Ben wants the assignment without naming what it costs him to be trusted with it alone. Neither of them opens the roster.
turning_point: Luke sets the datapad down and says, evenly, that he has felt something too. Ben hears the difference — his father is describing an anomaly; Ben is recognising a register he has lived inside since he was a boy.
opening_hook: Luke's datapad shows a string of survey reports flagged with the same anomaly — Force readings that do not match any known phenomenon
closing_hook: Ben accepts the mission without suggesting a partner. Luke does not push. Neither of them acknowledges what that choice means.
emotional_trajectory: Guarded attentiveness -> brief connection with Luke -> deliberate distance

stakes.personal: Ben's need to prove himself independently of the Skywalker name
stakes.interpersonal: The careful, love-laden distance between father and son
stakes.external: The survey route runs directly along the wrongness's bearing

setting: Luke's office in the Jedi Temple, Coruscant — functional, lived-in, holocomm on the desk
sensory_details: Luke's Force presence warm and familiar at close range; the datapad's blue glow on the desk between them; the wrongness carried even into this room as a faint sourness under the Temple's usual harmonics; ambient Coruscant traffic audible through the office window as a continuous low wash
canon_elements_needed: Luke Skywalker as Grand Master of the Jedi Order
Jedi Order survey mission protocols and assignment hierarchy
Luke and Ben Skywalker relationship post-Lost Tribe crisis
Force perception differences between Skywalker bloodline practitioners
Jedi Temple Grand Master administrative spaces
action_beats: Luke slides the datapad across the desk showing seventeen flagged survey reports
Ben scrolls through the anomaly data, zooming on three readings that match his own perception
Ben sets the datapad down and moves to the window — body language of someone accepting a solo mission
notes: The relationship turn here is Ben/Luke from institutional distance toward private alliance without yet closing the distance. Luke should feel warm but slightly formal — they love each other and communicate through mission briefings. Ben thinks 'Dad' internally and speaks to his father as a Knight addressing the Grand Master. Orientation — if Mara or Jacen surfaces in this scene, each earns one grounding phrase (Mara as 'his mother', Jacen as a weighted name that does not stop for a recap) and the sentence moves. No flashback paragraph. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben's interior read of Luke should stay reactive (what the man in front of him does and does not say, the pause before the pad slides across the desk), not an essay on the Skywalker shadow. If a line of interiority could stand alone as a clean declarative sentence about trust or legacy, cut it. Lived-galaxy texture — the office is in a working building on a working planet; Coruscant traffic and Order admin life can bleed through the edges of the scene without needing a set-piece.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Luke sets the datapad down and says, evenly, that he has felt something too.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben registers the difference in his father's register — Luke is describing an anomaly as a Grand Master would; Ben is recognizing a frequency he has lived inside since childhood. The wrongness is no longer Ben's private burden; it is now shared, but only between them, and only in this room.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben must accept the mission without naming what it costs him to be trusted alone with it. The careful, love-laden distance between father and son tightens rather than closes. Ben's need to prove himself independently of the Skywalker name is both honored and weaponized by Luke's trust.

emotional_arc.start: Guarded attentiveness — Ben enters the office braced for a routine briefing, not prepared to have his private reading validated by the Grand Master.
emotional_arc.shift: Brief connection with Luke — the moment Luke names the wrongness, Ben feels the pressure of being truly seen, the relief and terror of that recognition.
emotional_arc.end: Deliberate distance — Ben steps away from the desk toward the window, reasserting the boundary he needs to maintain. The connection is real; the distance is necessary.

key_beats.beat_description: Luke slides the datapad across the desk, showing seventeen flagged survey reports clustered along a bearing in the Outer Rim.
key_beats.state_change: The wrongness becomes concrete. Ben's private reading is now institutional fact — the Order has noticed.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's instinct pushes toward action rather than explanation. His body tightens; he reaches for the datapad before his mind has finished processing what the gesture means. The guarded attentiveness sharpens into focus.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben scrolls through the anomaly data, zooming on three readings that match his own independent perception — the same sourness in the Force-weave, the same wrongness he has been carrying for weeks.
key_beats.state_change: Validation and isolation collapse into the same moment. Ben is not alone in feeling this. Luke has been reading the same signals. But Luke's reading is clinical; Ben's is visceral. The gap between them is suddenly visible.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The pressure turns inward and upward — Ben feels the brief connection with Luke like a note played slightly flat, present but wrong. His focus tightens on what just changed in the room: his father sees the anomaly; Ben sees the wound. The distinction matters and cannot be named.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben sets the datapad down on the desk and moves to the window, his body language settling into the posture of someone accepting a solo assignment.
key_beats.state_change: Ben does not ask for a partner. Luke does not offer one. The mission is now Ben's alone, and the silence around that choice becomes the scene's weight.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Deliberate distance reasserts itself — Ben needs the window, the space, the physical separation. His shoulders settle into a readiness that is also a closing. The brief connection with Luke is real; the distance is necessary. Ben braces for the handoff.

anti_patterns: Ben's interior read of Luke should stay reactive (what the man in front of him does and does not say, the pause before the pad slides across the desk), not an essay on the Skywalker shadow
If a line of interiority could stand alone as a clean declarative sentence about trust or legacy, cut it
Do not arrive at diagnostic voice when describing the wrongness or the Force-weave — stay sensory and immediate
Avoid clinical articulation of Ben's emotional state; let it live in his body and his choices
